2. For every borough i, compute the simple spatial lag Lᵢ = mean(Energy_value of all listed neighbors of i).  
   • If a borough ever had an empty neighbor list we would drop it from the analysis, but every London borough in the supplied file has ≥1 neighbor, so no special handling is needed.

3. Build the city-wide baseline relationship by running an ordinary least-squares regression:
      Energy_valueᵢ  =  α  +  β · Lᵢ  +  εᵢ
   Store the fitted values ŷᵢ and raw residuals rᵢ = εᵢ.

4. Apply the ITERATIVE-R masking-robust procedure (Lu, Chen & Kou, 2003) to the residuals:  
   a. Initialize the working set W with all 33 boroughs.  
   b. Fit the regression in Step 3 using only W and compute standardized residuals zᵢ = rᵢ / s, where s is the sample standard deviation of residuals in W.  
   c. Remove from W every borough whose |zᵢ| > 2.5 (a commonly recommended ITERATIVE-R cutoff).  
   d. Repeat b–c until no additional boroughs are dropped.  
   e. The final regression coefficients α*, β* and standard deviation s* come from the last iteration’s model.

5. Using α*, β*, and s*, calculate City of London’s final standardized residual z_CoL = (Energy_value_CoL – (α* + β* · L_CoL)) / s*.

6. Declare the outlier status for City of London:  
   • If |z_CoL| > 2.5 → spatial outlier (label as OUTLIER – HIGH if z_CoL > 0, OUTLIER – LOW if z_CoL < 0).  
   • Otherwise → NOT AN OUTLIER.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import defaultdict

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
ENERGY_PATH = "chunks_csv/outlierr/2022_energy.csv"
ADJ_PATH    = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df_energy = pd.read_csv(ENERGY_PATH)          # columns: borough, Energy_value
df_adj    = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)             # columns: borough, neighbor

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build undirected neighbour dictionary
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
neigh = defaultdict(set)
for _, row in df_adj.iterrows():
    a, b = row["borough"], row["neighbor"]
    neigh[a].add(b)
    neigh[b].add(a)          # ensure symmetry

# Sanity-check: every borough must have ≥1 neighbour
assert all(len(neigh[b]) > 0 for b in df_energy["borough"]), "A borough has no neighbours!"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Compute spatial lag L_i  =  mean( neighbours’ Energy_value )
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
energy_dict = dict(zip(df_energy["borough"], df_energy["Energy_value"]))

L_values = []
for bor in df_energy["borough"]:
    L_values.append( np.mean([energy_dict[n] for n in neigh[bor]]) )

df_energy["Lag"] = L_values

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. ITERATIVE-R procedure (Lu, Chen & Kou, 2003)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
current_set = df_energy.index.copy()    # start with all 33 observations
cutoff      = 2.5                       # |z| threshold

while True:
    # Fit OLS:  Energy = alpha + beta * Lag     using current_set
    Y = df_energy.loc[current_set, "Energy_value"].to_numpy()
    X = np.column_stack((np.ones(len(current_set)), df_energy.loc[current_set, "Lag"]))
    beta_hat, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, Y, rcond=None)   # [alpha, beta]
    y_hat  = X @ beta_hat
    resid  = Y - y_hat
    s      = resid.std(ddof=1)

    z_scores = resid / s
    outlier_mask = np.abs(z_scores) > cutoff
    if not outlier_mask.any():
        # Converged – no more points removed
        break
    # drop the detected outliers and iterate
    current_set = current_set[~outlier_mask]

# Store final model parameters
alpha_final, beta_final = beta_hat
s_final                 = s
final_indices           = current_set            # boroughs kept in the final fit

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Compute City of London’s final standardized residual
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
city = "City of London"
energy_col = energy_dict[city]
lag_col    = np.mean([energy_dict[n] for n in neigh[city]])

pred_city  = alpha_final + beta_final * lag_col
z_city     = (energy_col - pred_city) / s_final

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Decide outlier status
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if np.abs(z_city) > cutoff:
    verdict = "OUTLIER - HIGH" if z_city > 0 else "OUTLIER - LOW"
else:
    verdict = "NOT AN OUTLIER"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Reporting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
data_points_used = len(df_energy)   # 33 rows, none missing

print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (z = {z_city:.3f})")
